title: Fixed-degree pseudo-coherence is independent of the polynomial presentation
statement: Let $R,A$ be commutative rings, let $r,s\geq0$, and let $\alpha:P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_r]\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $\beta:Q=R[y_1,\ldots,y_s]\twoheadrightarrow A$ be surjective $R$-algebra homomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For every $m\in\mathbf Z$ and $K\in D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $$\alpha_*K\text{ is }m\text{-pseudo-coherent over }P\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\beta_*K\text{ is }m\text{-pseudo-coherent over }Q$$ [def-pc-ring-m-pseudo-coherent]. Restriction of scalars is termwise, with identical additive groups and differentials and scalar action through the displayed map; it is exact and preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Zero variables and zero rings are allowed. No flatness, finite presentation, Noetherian, or cohomological boundedness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 065H, lemma-relatively-pseudo-coherent, equivalence (1) and (2) for a fixed integer m.

proof.text: For a commutative ring $B$ and $b\in B$, evaluation $e_b:B[t]\to B$ has the exact sequence $0\to B[t]\xrightarrow{t-b}B[t]\xrightarrow{e_b}B\to0$. Constants show surjectivity. The identity $t^a-b^a=(t-b)\sum_{h=0}^{a-1}t^{a-1-h}b^h$ for $a>0$ shows that $p(t)-p(b)$ is divisible by $t-b$, so the kernel is its image. Multiplication by $t-b$ is injective: if a nonzero polynomial has highest nonzero coefficient $c$ in degree $d$, its product has coefficient $c$ in degree $d+1$. Hence $[B[t]\xrightarrow{t-b}B[t]]$ in degrees $-1,0$ is a bounded finite free model for $B[0]$. By the definition, $B[0]$ is pseudo-coherent over $B[t]$. For the zero ring the same sequence is the zero exact sequence.

source.place: Tag 065G, lemma-add-variable-pseudo-coherent, first proof and displayed exact sequence; explicit evaluation-at-b version

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-m-pseudocoherent-algebra-scalar-restriction] with $S=B[t]$, $T=B$, and $f=e_b$. Step 1 verifies exactly its hypothesis that $T[0]$ is pseudo-coherent over $S$. Thus for every integer $m$ and every $L\in D(B)$, $L$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent over $B$ if and only if $(e_b)_*L$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent over $B[t]$. The degree $m$ is unchanged, and no bound on $L$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 065G, lemma-add-variable-pseudo-coherent, first sentence applying Tag 064Z, lemma-finite-push-pseudo-coherent, fixed-m equivalence

proof.text: Choose lifts $f_j\in P$ of $\beta(y_j)$ through $\alpha$, and $g_i\in Q$ of $\alpha(x_i)$ through $\beta$. Set $T=R[x_1,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_s]$. Define $u:T\to P$ by $x_i\mapsto x_i$, $y_j\mapsto f_j$, and $v:T\to Q$ by $y_j\mapsto y_j$, $x_i\mapsto g_i$. By the polynomial universal property, $\alpha\circ u=\beta\circ v=: \gamma$, since these maps agree on every variable. The same property identifies $T$ with $P[y_1,\ldots,y_s]$ and with $Q[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$: the maps fixing the displayed variables are inverse. On a representative of $K$, restriction along either composite gives the identical $T$-action through $\gamma$, with unchanged groups and differentials. Thus $u_*\alpha_*K=\gamma_*K=v_*\beta_*K$ in $D(T)$.

source.place: Tag 065H, lemma-relatively-pseudo-coherent, lifts and common polynomial ring diagram

proof.text: For $0\leq j\leq s$ put $P_j=P[y_1,\ldots,y_j]$, and let $L_j$ be a representative of $\alpha_*K$ with $y_a$ acting by $f_a$ for $a\leq j$. The base $L_0$ is $\alpha_*K$. For $j\geq1$, $L_j$ is the restriction of $L_{j-1}$ along $P_{j-1}[y_j]\to P_{j-1}$ evaluating $y_j$ at $f_j\in P\subset P_{j-1}$. Step 2, namely [lem-sfb-m-pseudocoherent-algebra-scalar-restriction] with the resolution from step 1, gives equivalence of $m$-pseudo-coherence at each successor. Induction gives equivalence between $\alpha_*K$ over $P$ and $L_s=\gamma_*K$ over $T$. For the other presentation put $Q_i=Q[x_1,\ldots,x_i]$ for $0\leq i\leq r$ and let $N_i$ be a representative of $\beta_*K$ with $x_a$ acting by $g_a$ for $a\leq i$. Start with $N_0=\beta_*K$; at successor $i$ evaluate $x_i$ at $g_i\in Q\subset Q_{i-1}$ and apply step 2. This gives equivalence between $\beta_*K$ over $Q$ and $N_r=\gamma_*K$ over $T$. Combining proves the assertion for the same fixed $m$. If $r=0$ or $s=0$, that induction has only its base case.
